## Statement

Identification is a property of the observed data together with the assumptions, not a property of the estimator. A neural network cannot learn a counterfactual contrast that the data and assumptions do not identify, and flexible modeling that reduces approximation error in a nuisance function can at the same time disguise unsupported extrapolation, because a smooth fit extends confidently into regions with no observations. The distinction is stated clearly in the methodological literature and is repeatedly elided in applied work, where a more flexible learner is offered as the answer to a confounding or positivity concern. There is no diagnostic in common use that separates a flexible model interpolating where data exist from the same model extrapolating where they do not.

## Why it is open

Extrapolation is not visible in any conventional fit statistic: a model can have excellent cross-validated loss on the observed region and be entirely unconstrained off it. The regions that matter are conditional on a growing treatment and covariate history, so the question of whether a given prediction is supported is itself high-dimensional. The professional incentive also points one way, since the flexible estimate is the one with the tighter interval.

## What has been tried

::: {.table-scroll}

| Work | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| [Feuerriegel S, Frauen D, Melnychuk V, et al. Causal machine learning for predicting treatment outcomes. Nat Med 2024;30:958-968](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-024-02902-1) | States that causal machine learning supports individualized effect estimation only under the same identification assumptions as conventional methods, which is the claim applied work elides. |
| [Target trial emulation under nonmutually exclusive assignment. Am J Epidemiol 2026;195(4):1045](https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwaf018) | Demonstrates empirically that poor overlap defeats advanced adjustment, which is the concrete form the general point takes. |

:::

## Probable solution or research direction

Require that any flexible nuisance model be paired with a support diagnostic reported for the same conditioning sets the model uses, so extrapolation is visible where it happens rather than aggregated away. Score estimators on failure awareness: whether their diagnostics correctly signal a severe positivity violation or a non-identifiable target, tested against deliberately non-identifiable simulation scenarios. Include at least one such scenario in every methods comparison, since an estimator that always returns a narrow interval is not robust if it never warns.

## Verification

::: {.verification-trail}
**Verdict.** Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.

**Dissent.** literature dissented (supported): The corpus contains a growing body of flexible estimation inside emulations, including ensemble-learning marginal structural models and deep learning comparisons, and it contains no support diagnostic reported alongside a flexible nuisance model and no methods comparison that includes a deliberately non-identifiable scenario. A 2026 Nature Communications paper evaluates bias across statistical and deep learning methods in a heart failure emulation, which is the comparison the entry wants and does not include a non-identifiable arm. Failure awareness as a scored property does not appear anywhere.

4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check
:   **open / supported.** The corpus contains a growing body of flexible estimation inside emulations, including ensemble-learning marginal structural models and deep learning comparisons, and it contains no support diagnostic reported alongside a flexible nuisance model and no methods comparison that includes a deliberately non-identifiable scenario. A 2026 Nature Communications paper evaluates bias across statistical and deep learning methods in a heart failure emulation, which is the comparison the entry wants and does not include a non-identifiable arm. Failure awareness as a scored property does not appear anywhere.
    Cites 10.1038/s41467-026-74999-6: Compares flexible against conventional estimation for bias inside an emulation, which is the nearest existing test and does not include a non-identifiable scenario..
    Cites 10.1002/bimj.70133: Applies ensemble learning to the weight model in a longitudinal setting, which is where the extrapolation concern applies..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens
:   **open / overstated.** The central identification claim is correct, although identification formally concerns the observed-data law, causal model, target estimand, and identifying assumptions rather than the realized finite dataset. Flexible estimation cannot repair failed exchangeability or positivity. The absolute diagnostic claim is too strong: propensity-score overlap, conditional treatment probabilities, density ratios, nearest-neighbor distances, leverage, and related support diagnostics can operationally flag extrapolation. They cannot certify identification, diagnose unmeasured confounding, or provide a model-free boundary between interpolation and extrapolation in high-dimensional longitudinal histories. Simulations can test warnings for deliberately detectable support failures, but no estimator can be required to detect every nonidentifiable target from the observed distribution alone. No package capability claim is present.

Grok 4.5, recency lens
:   **open / supported-with-caveat.** Inverted search did not find a standard that closes this gap. Feuerriegel et al. (Nat Med 2024) restate that causal ML requires the same identification assumptions as classical methods and does not identify contrasts the data cannot support; that is prior art for the claim, not a solution. Hill and Su (Ann Appl Stat 2013) and Nethery et al. (Ann Appl Stat 2019) give BART-centered common-support diagnostics and nonoverlap-aware estimation, and propensity-score density/trim diagnostics remain routine for low-dimensional scores. Those tools do not constitute a diagnostic in common use that flags, for a general flexible nuisance (including neural nets) and for the same high-dimensional conditioning sets the nuisance uses, which predictions are interpolation versus extrapolation. Package activity in TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, lmtp, WeightIt, and related tools still emphasizes IPW weight extremity and classical overlap plots rather than per-prediction support maps for flexible outcome models. Failure-awareness scoring against deliberately non-identifiable simulations is not an established methods-comparison standard. The problem remains open as stated for applied flexible nuisance work; the caveat is that specialized support diagnostics for some nonparametric models already exist and should be named rather than implied to be nonexistent.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens
:   **open / supported.** The claim correctly identifies that identification is a property of data and assumptions, not the estimator, and that flexible models can disguise extrapolation. The reason given for it being open (lack of common diagnostics for high-dimensional extrapolation) logically supports the claim. The claim is pitched at the right level of generality and correctly frames the issue as a current practice gap rather than a structural impossibility.

Decision path
:   `R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex`

:::

## How the evidence falls in time

38 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2010 to 2026. Partial progress is on the record, and later work still calls this open. Both belong in view.

This problem is **recurrent**: three or more papers spanning at least eight years assert it independently. Sustained restatement by authors who mostly do not cite each other is the strongest evidence this reading can offer that a gap is real rather than one group's framing.
